explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. The psalm says, "Not to us, O LORD, not to us, but to Your name be the glory…" (Psalm 115:1). It says "Not to us…" twice, like it really wants to be sure we heard. The credit goes up, not back to the people praying.

Good guess, but the psalm never mentions the heavenly host. It says, "Not to us, O LORD, not to us, but to Your name be the glory…" (Psalm 115:1). The glory goes to the LORD's name. The psalm doesn't send it anywhere else.

The temple is a fine place, friend, but it isn't where the psalm sends the glory. Look at the line: "Not to us, O LORD, not to us, but to Your name be the glory…" (Psalm 115:1). The glory goes to the LORD's name, not to a building.

Yes, baker. The psalm says the glory goes to His name "…because of Your loving devotion, because of Your faithfulness." (Psalm 115:1). The reason is who He is. It isn't a thank-you for anything we did.

explanations.answer: His people's hard work and gifts
explanations.explanation: Hold on, friend. The psalm just said "Not to us…" so the glory isn't about our hard work. It says the glory goes to His name "…because of Your loving devotion, because of Your faithfulness." (Psalm 115:1). The reason is Him, not our effort.

The psalm doesn't mention the temple here at all. It gives the reason in plain words: "…because of Your loving devotion, because of Your faithfulness." (Psalm 115:1). Loving devotion and faithfulness are who He is, no gold needed.
That's right, baker. The psalm says, "Our God is in heaven; He does as He pleases." (Psalm 115:3). The nations ask where He is, and the psalm answers in one short line. No long speech needed.
Close, but the psalm doesn't say that here. It answers the nations' question with "Our God is in heaven; He does as He pleases." (Psalm 115:3). The answer is heaven, plain and simple.

Mount Sinai is a big one in the Bible, friend, but the psalm doesn't bring it up. Its answer to the nations is "Our God is in heaven; He does as He pleases." (Psalm 115:3). Heaven is where the psalm puts Him.
Not quite, baker. The psalm says, "Our God is in heaven; He does as He pleases." (Psalm 115:3). Nobody sits above Him telling Him what to do. Doing as He pleases means the decision is His.
Right, friend. The psalm says, "Our God is in heaven; He does as He pleases." (Psalm 115:3). Nobody else decides what He does. The decision is His.
Yes, baker. The psalm says, "Their idols are silver and gold, made by the hands of men." (Psalm 115:4). People made them. Silver and gold, and still made by hands.
The psalm says the opposite, friend. It says, "Their idols are silver and gold, made by the hands of men." (Psalm 115:4). The idols come from human hands. They shine, but people made them.
Careful, baker. The psalm says the idols have eyes, but it adds "…but cannot see…" (Psalm 115:5). Having eyes and seeing are two different things. These idols have the first one only.
Right, friend. The psalm says, "they have eyes, but cannot see…" (Psalm 115:5). The eyes are there, but they don't work. It's like a timer with a face and no tick.

That's right, baker. The psalm says, "Those who make them become like them…" (Psalm 115:8). The verse also says the same of "…all who trust in them." The psalm doesn't spell out how they become like them, so I'll leave it there.
Not here, friend. The psalm says, "Those who make them become like them…" (Psalm 115:8). The idols can't see, hear or walk, so being like them is no step up. Wise and strong isn't in the verse.
The psalm doesn't say anything about long lives for idol makers. It says, "Those who make them become like them…" (Psalm 115:8). And after the list of what the idols can't do, that's no great deal.

Look again, baker. The verse says, "Those who make them become like them, as do all who trust in them." (Psalm 115:8). It names two groups: the makers and everyone who trusts in the idols. Trusting in them counts too.
Yes, friend. The psalm says, "Those who make them become like them, as do all who trust in them." (Psalm 115:8). It's not only the makers. All who trust in the idols are included.

That's it, baker. The psalm says, "O Israel, trust in the LORD! He is their help and shield." (Psalm 115:9). Help and shield, two jobs in one line. Compare that to idols that can't even clear their throats.
Those are big titles, friend, but they aren't in this verse. The psalm says, "O Israel, trust in the LORD! He is their help and shield." (Psalm 115:9). Help and shield is the line to remember.
That sounds nice, baker, but it isn't what the psalm says. It says, "O Israel, trust in the LORD! He is their help and shield." (Psalm 115:9). He's their help and shield.

explanations.answer: The house of Aaron and those who fear the LORD
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. After Israel, the psalm calls out "O house of Aaron…" and then "You who fear the LORD…" (Psalm 115:10-11). Each call ends the same way: "He is their help and shield." Three groups, one LORD to trust.

explanations.answer: The kings of Judah and the prophets of Israel
explanations.explanation: Not those two, friend. The psalm calls out "O house of Aaron…" and "You who fear the LORD…" (Psalm 115:10-11). Kings and prophets aren't named in these verses. The call to trust stays the same for every group.

explanations.answer: The elders of the land and the judges of Israel
explanations.explanation: Good try, baker, but the psalm doesn't name them. It calls out "O house of Aaron…" and "You who fear the LORD…" (Psalm 115:10-11). Elders and judges aren't in these verses.
That's right, baker. The psalm says, "He will bless those who fear the LORD—small and great alike." (Psalm 115:13). Small and great are both covered. Nobody gets left out for being too little.

Not quite, friend. The verse says, "He will bless those who fear the LORD—small and great alike." (Psalm 115:13). Small is the word that fits. The blessing is for those who fear the LORD, small and great.

Money isn't what the psalm names, baker. It says, "He will bless those who fear the LORD—small and great alike." (Psalm 115:13). The word is small. The blessing is for those who fear the LORD, small and great.
Yes, baker. The psalm says, "May the LORD give you increase, both you and your children." (Psalm 115:14). The blessing covers the listeners and their children. Both are in the prayer.
Look at the line again, friend. The psalm says, "May the LORD give you increase, both you and your children." (Psalm 115:14). Both you and your children. The blessing reaches them too.

explanations.answer: The Maker of heaven and earth
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. The psalm says, "May you be blessed by the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth." (Psalm 115:15). The One blessing you is the One who made everything. The idols were made by hands, and He made the heavens.
Close in spirit, friend, but not the title here. The psalm says, "May you be blessed by the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth." (Psalm 115:15). Maker of heaven and earth is the one to remember.
That one isn't in this verse, baker. The psalm says, "May you be blessed by the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth." (Psalm 115:15). His title here is Maker of heaven and earth.
Yes, baker. The psalm says, "The highest heavens belong to the LORD, but the earth He has given to mankind." (Psalm 115:16). The heavens are His, and the earth is given to mankind. That's a big gift.
Not priests, friend. The psalm says, "The highest heavens belong to the LORD, but the earth He has given to mankind." (Psalm 115:16). The earth was given to all mankind, not just one group.

Kings are a fun guess, baker, but they're not in this verse. The psalm says, "The highest heavens belong to the LORD, but the earth He has given to mankind." (Psalm 115:16). The earth goes to mankind.

That's right, baker. The psalm says, "But it is we who will bless the LORD, both now and forevermore." (Psalm 115:18). The line right before says the dead don't praise Him. So "we" is the voice of the psalm.
The angels aren't mentioned here, friend. The psalm says, "But it is we who will bless the LORD, both now and forevermore." (Psalm 115:18). The "we" is the people speaking in the psalm.

Not the answer here, baker. Earlier, the nations were the ones asking "Where is their God?" (Psalm 115:2). The psalm says, "But it is we who will bless the LORD, both now and forevermore." (Psalm 115:18). The "we" is the voice speaking in the psalm.
Check the ending, baker. The psalm says, "But it is we who will bless the LORD, both now and forevermore." (Psalm 115:18). Forevermore means no stopping point. Now and forever, both.
Right, friend. The psalm says, "But it is we who will bless the LORD, both now and forevermore." (Psalm 115:18). It's now and forevermore. There's no stopping point in that line.
